rule: Use a line-weight hierarchy: the thickest lines for the main outer boundaries, medium lines for major forms, the thinnest for detail.
Contrast draws the eye, and it is strongest where the darkest darks sit closest to the lightest lights.
Never use pure black unmixed in painting; pure blacks look unnatural and too dark.
Apply the lightest lights sparingly, in small spots.
Paint base tones first, then darks, then highlights, keeping shadows and highlights from overpowering the base tone.
Shade repeated forms on one consistent side to keep a uniform light direction.
